call_points.text: Small-town network delivered its 6th consecutive quarter of double-digit LTL growth.
Added 100+ stores in Q2, the highest in over 2 years, with 86 net additions in H1.
Own e-commerce business grew 70% in Q2, supported by enhanced hyperlocal capabilities.
Launched 'Vybe by Peter England' to target Gen Z consumers.
call_points.versus_prior: addressing previous analyst concern on Gen-Z strategy

call_points.text: Reebok reached a milestone with its 250th store opening.
call_points.versus_prior: on track for long-term growth target

call_points.text: Gross margin fell about 150 bps YoY on channel mix and higher provisioning; management called it not material.
Marketing spend was about 3.5% of sales, lower YoY as the company moved from IPL to digital advertising.
Apparel is now 32-33% of Reebok, up from 26-27% at acquisition; women's wear remains small.
BIS approval for imported Reebok factories remains an annual renewal issue; the company is diversifying sourcing domestically.
Karnataka's minimum wage hike excludes garmenting, and manufacturing is about 40% of production, spread across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
Quick commerce is still a very small part of the business, led by innerwear.
Company targets a steady-state retail like-for-like (LTL) growth of **~7%** over the next few years across Lifestyle Brands.
call_points.versus_prior: FY26 full year retail LTL was 9%

call_points.text: Van Heusen Innerwear is targeted to deliver at least one profitable quarter during **FY27**.
Management expects operating cash flows should ideally make the company **debt-free** within the next three years.
In Q4FY26, the company recognized a one-off **₹20 Cr PLI benefit** in its manufacturing subsidiary in Pulivendula.
Company plans fewer store closures this year after heavy consolidation in FY26, supporting higher net additions.
Retail like-to-like growth reached 9% for ABLBL in FY26, with double-digit L2L growth in small towns.
Van Heusen Innerwear recorded 30% retail LTL growth in FY26 and is on path to breakeven.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,174.16 Cr, net profit ₹54.52 Cr.
ABLBL released Q4 and FY26 investor presentation detailing 7% FY26 revenue growth to ₹8,396 Cr and 300+ gross store additions.
ABLBL held its Q4FY26 earnings call, guiding FY27 capex to ₹250-300 Cr, ~7% steady retail LTL growth, and targeting debt freedom in 3 years.
Birla Group Holdings Private Limited, as promoter, declared no new encumbrances on Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited shares by 31-Mar-2026.
Q1FY27 earnings call (Aug 3, 2026): revenue ₹2,046 Cr, up 11% YoY; EBITDA ₹327 Cr, margin 16%; PAT ₹29 Cr, up 21%; 68 gross stores added, network at 3,362.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,265.61 Cr (+11.2% YoY), net profit ₹53.05 Cr (+126.3% YoY).
ABLBL reported Q2FY27 revenue growth of 11% YoY to ₹2,266 Cr and a 126% jump in PAT to ₹53 Cr, driven by strong performance in the Emerging Business segment.
